clue.text: Orders given during street 'riots?

parts.note: in, as in 'in the night', means during
ructions are noisy disturbances or rows

explanation.surface: Commands are shouted out while a street erupts in riots.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'street riots' with no apostrophe; the mark in the held text is a speck on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Instructions are directions to be obeyed, the plural noun sense matching orders as commands.

clue.text: Jeremiah's book absorbed by one so religious?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: something absorbed by another is taken inside it

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus
Lam is the abbreviation for Lamentations, the book traditionally credited to Jeremiah

explanation.surface: Someone reading Jeremiah's book so deeply must be devout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed by' places LAM inside ISIC. The question mark flags that Islamic is only one kind of religious.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamic means relating to Islam, an example of a religious description, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Is noticeably more prominent? Adulation stems from that

indicators.note: says the words before come from rearranging the answer, so their letters are shuffled back

explanation.surface: Someone stands out so much that praise flows from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'Adulation stems' are an anagram of the answer, and 'from that' says they derive from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand out a mile is the idiom for being extremely conspicuous.

clue.text: Cook in pan

explanation.surface: A recipe telling you to cook in a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pan' looks like a utensil, but here it is the verb to criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to cook in an oven, and also to criticise someone severely, as critics pan a play.

clue.text: Maiden comes into make a meal in the afternoon

indicators.note: one letter coming into a word is placed inside it

parts.note: to create is to make
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman drops in to prepare an afternoon meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes into' puts M inside CREATE, then A. A cream tea is the British afternoon treat of scones, jam, clotted cream and tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is a light afternoon meal of tea with scones, jam and cream.

clue.text: Be cross, having first got one's goat

indicators.note: says the numeral comes at the front of the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Someone is angry because a person has taken their goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got one's goat' suggests annoyance, but goat is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat with long curved horns.

clue.text: Musical director ultimately ran up an account

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the whole run of letters is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Evita is a stage musical

indicators.note: points to the last letter of director

explanation.surface: A musical director has run up a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical director' reads as one conductor, but it is a show plus the last letter of director; 'up' reverses the run in this down entry, giving ATIVE R NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account or story of events.

clue.text: Ruthlessly pursue one's aim, or be a drifter?

explanation.surface: Someone single-minded or a drifter, two opposite lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: a drifter stays with nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick at nothing is to let no scruple stop you, and read literally it means to stay with nothing.

clue.text: Car is all the deceased owned

explanation.surface: A car is everything the dead person left.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a car with a long back for luggage, and also the whole property of someone who has died.

clue.text: Climbing plant twisted round a spike

indicators.note: something twisted round faces the other way, so the word for a spike is read backwards

parts.note: a nail is a metal spike

explanation.surface: A climbing plant has wound itself round a garden spike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted round' gives LIAN. 'spike' tempts as a plant part, but it is the hardware sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody vine of tropical forests that climbs up trees.

clue.text: Hates business manager's charges

parts.note: an exec, short for executive, is a business manager
rates are charges or fees

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the fees their business manager bills them.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to detest or curse, the third-person verb matching hates.

clue.text: Found an opportunity to give out cheese rolls

indicators.note: something that rolls over turns end to end, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: to emit is to give out
Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: Someone found a moment to hand round some cheese rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' looks like bread but turns EMIT plus EDAM backwards: MADE then TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To make time for something is the idiom for finding a chance or slot to do it.

clue.text: Woman circulating top class stuff

indicators.note: going round means the joined letters are turned back to front

parts.note: A1, read as AI, means first-rate
to cram is to stuff

explanation.surface: A woman is passing round some first-rate material.
explanation.walkthrough: AI stands for A1, top class; 'circulating' reverses AICRAM to give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcia is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Fail to get into our class at first, being more dull

indicators.note: says the class abbreviation is placed at the front of the answer

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class

indicators.note: one word getting into another sits inside it, so die goes inside our

parts.note: to die is to fail, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: Missing a place in our class at the start leaves someone gloomier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' sends the class abbreviation to the front; 'to get into' gives OUDIER. 'Fail' looks like flunking a class but means to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloudier skies are greyer and duller, a comparative adjective like more dull.

clue.text: Quantity of liquid — declare it's fermenting

indicators.note: something fermenting bubbles and churns, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: it, with the apostrophe s standing for is

explanation.surface: Announce that the liquid is brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fermenting' rearranges DECLARE IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A decalitre is ten litres, a measure of liquid volume.

clue.text: Drink a variety of retsina after opening

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters are rearranged
means once the opening letter has been removed from retsina

explanation.surface: A drink made from some other kind of retsina, served once uncorked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after opening' drops the R of retsina, and 'a variety of' rearranges ETSINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is an infusion of herbs, a kind of herbal tea to drink.

clue.text: Cheeky individual in pub sitting on top of table

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece sitting on another lies above it
one word in another sits inside it

parts.note: an inn is a pub
sole means single or individual

indicators.note: points to the first letter of table

explanation.surface: A cheeky person at the pub perches on a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sitting on' works because in a down answer the earlier letters sit above the later ones; 'in' builds INSOLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means rude and disrespectful, a stronger form of cheeky.

clue.text: Revolt as school place is reversed

indicators.note: says the two pieces swap their order, so place comes before school

parts.note: to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: Pupils rebel because their school has been turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is reversed' swaps the order of the two pieces rather than turning letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden attempt to overthrow a government, a kind of uprising.

clue.text: Cake portion cut and given to family

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its last letter

parts.note: a part is a portion
kin are family

explanation.surface: A slice of cake is cut and handed to relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims PART to PAR. Parkin is a ginger and oatmeal cake from northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkin is a sticky gingerbread cake made with oatmeal and treacle.

clue.text: Suspect held in revolution, say, seen to abandon extremes

indicators.note: signals that the word for revolution is only heard, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a turn is one revolution

indicators.note: means dropping the first and last letters of seen

explanation.surface: Someone suspected is detained during an uprising, and seems to give up on radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives TERN for TURN; 'to abandon extremes' leaves EE from seen.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is a person confined, often without trial, as someone held under suspicion.

clue.text: Mountain engulfed in severe storm

indicators.note: something engulfed in words is swallowed up inside them

explanation.surface: A mountain is swallowed by a fierce storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the highest mountain in the world.

clue.text: Discover convention includes mass taken by bishop

indicators.note: one word including others holds them inside

parts.note: a rule is an accepted convention

indicators.note: says the mass letter is taken along by the bishop letter, placed beside it

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Church custom is uncovered when a bishop celebrates mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts MB inside RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rumble someone is British slang for finding them out, so it means to discover.

clue.text: Flirt, right to be banned from ball, of 'course

indicators.note: something banned from a place is taken out of it, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: a croquette is a fried ball of food served as a course

explanation.surface: A flirt is barred from the dance, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance and 'of course' an aside; together they mean a croquette, from which 'to be banned from' removes R. The apostrophe is a speck on the scan.
explanation.definitionFit: A coquette is a woman who flirts, so the noun matches flirt.

clue.text: Law of our country, so to speak

indicators.note: signals that the words are said aloud and spelt as they sound

parts.note: for a British setter our country is the UK, so belonging to it is the UK's

explanation.surface: The law of our nation, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' turns UK's, said aloud, into a sound-alike word. A ukase was a decree of the Russian tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase is an edict or decree having the force of law, originally from the Russian tsar.

clue.text: Prepared diversion

explanation.surface: A planned piece of entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Game means willing or ready to do something, and a game is an amusement or pastime.

clue.text: Next to a 21, I shall appear uncomfortable

indicators.note: says the contraction stands beside the other pieces

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I shall
refers to the answer at 21 across, a flirt, which is also a tease

explanation.surface: Sitting beside a flirt, I'll feel awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' points to the flirt clue, and a flirt is a tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill at ease is the idiom for feeling awkward or uncomfortable.

clue.text: A tree house finally in flames

parts.note: a fir is a tree

indicators.note: points to the last letter of house

explanation.surface: A treehouse is burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Afire means burning, an adjective matching in flames.

clue.text: Too many trombones, for the record?

explanation.surface: A band has more trombones than it needs, for the record.
explanation.walkthrough: '76 Trombones' is a song from The Music Man, so one more would be too many... and two more is 78. A 78 is an old gramophone record, from its speed of 78 rpm.
explanation.definitionFit: A 78 is an old shellac record, and the number exceeds the 76 trombones of the famous song.
